in_repo_version_transition.mechanism: direct dependency; bump AND fix in the same commit
in_repo_version_transition.evidence: Commit 7ec771e ('update xstream dependency') bumps xstream 1.4.17 -> 1.4.19 (crossing the 1.4.18 default-deny boundary) and adds the allowTypes fix in the same commit (bump_and_fix_in_same_commit). A genuine adaptation-to-a-change.

bump_source.comment: BUMP is where the break was CONFIRMED (a dependabot PR that broke CI). The adaptation below is a separate maintainer commit.

behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: xstream 1.4.18 switched its security framework to default-deny: classes not on an explicit allowlist are rejected on deserialization. The client code still COMPILES against 1.4.19 (no API change) but throws ForbiddenClassException at runtime -> behavioural break, not syntactic.

adaptation.author: Robert Middleton
adaptation.production_usages_unfixed: ~10 XStream usages in src/main (ApplicationPreferenceModelSaver, ChainsawTabbedPane, LogPanel, MRUFileList, ZeroConfPlugin) were NOT given allowTypes; only the failing test was fixed. Project later removed xstream entirely.
adaptation.summary: Added the deserialized class to xstream's allowlist via XStream.allowTypes(...) to satisfy the new default-deny security model. NOTE: applied ONLY in the failing test; production code left unadapted (see production_usages_unfixed) — a partial/test-only adaptation.

verification.method: 3-state differential build+test with Maven on JDK 11, targeting the failing test only
verification.conclusion: Confirmed BBC: a passing test breaks only under the new library version with otherwise-unchanged code, and the client's adaptation resolves it.
